        A Shared Causal-Analysis Product
Investment and construction proposal for a universal bank


       Companion to Causal Inference for a Universal Bank

                        10 October 2026
The investment decision

A universal bank repeatedly needs to distinguish the effect of its actions from customer
selection, market conditions and the way information was recorded. A retention offer may
raise balances while reducing contribution. A collections policy may change future distress and
therefore the customers eligible for later assistance. A fitted latent-state model may forecast
well while attributing a private officer’s information to the bank’s action. These are scientific
and economic problems before they are software problems.
   The proposal is a common causal-analysis library with three standalone workspaces: in-
tervention studies, sequential decisions and dynamic systems. They share explicit targets,
historical information, identification arguments, uncertainty and reproducible evidence. The
product composes qualified open-source methods and supplies the scientific interfaces and data
semantics that ordinary estimator calls leave to each project. It does not promise automatic
identification from an arbitrary bank table.
   The recommended investment is a staged construction and comparison exercise. The first six-
month tranche has an illustrative USD 1.14 million envelope within an illustrative USD 4 million
total initial build. Its output is a small set of qualified operations, end-to-end demonstrations in
all three workspaces and measured comparison with expert composition. Expansion depends on
preserving analytical quality and finding enough repeated work to cover the shared cost. Under
the stated three-year account, cost-only break-even requires approximately 26.74 equivalent
completed studies per year. This is a consequence of assumptions, not measured bank demand.
   The accompanying monograph derives the scientific scope, compares primary literature and
44 open-source projects, and reports reproducible synthetic studies together with archived
household-finance and dynamic monetary-data applications. Preserved source copies and
inspected anchors support the citations. The proposal includes local reference implementations
and selected installed software-operation checks. It is not a deployed product. Institutional
data validation, full application workspaces and accepted sibling adoption remain construction
work.




                                                 ii
Chapter 1

What can be shared across banking
decisions

The reusable unit is a scientific request: a causal model, observation process, feasible in-
tervention, target population and outcome, sampling experiment, and information available
to the decision rule. The same request follows the analysis from data reconstruction to a
decision account. An invitation, acceptance of that invitation and the customer’s later balance
are different variables. Conditioning on acceptance can change both the population and the
meaning of the effect.
   The mathematical foundations determine the product’s shape. Causal diagrams encode
restrictions on assignments and mechanisms; identification determines whether those restrictions
imply a unique answer. Instrumental variables can identify a complier effect under specified
assumptions without identifying the population average effect (Angrist et al., 1996). Machine
learning can estimate the nuisance regressions in an orthogonal score, but it cannot supply
a missing exclusion or remove a weak instrument (Chernozhukov et al., 2018; Staiger and
Stock, 1994). Longitudinal methods additionally require an ordered decision history and
policy-specific support. A hidden-state representation adds a likelihood and a filtering problem,
while causal policy evaluation still needs an identification argument.
   The scientific result can therefore be an identified functional, an identified set, a conser-
vative bound, a nonidentification witness, an unsupported computation, or an incompatible
specification. These outcomes must remain distinct. A confidence set may be disconnected or
unbounded. A discovered graph may retain unresolved endpoints. A posterior over parameters
is conditional on its model; it is not automatically uncertainty over all compatible causal
mechanisms.
   The first catalogue contains seven bounded operation families: adjusted single-decision
effects; encouragement and IV contrasts; cohort and panel effects; history-policy values;
normalized structural shock responses; controlled latent-model analysis; and discovery followed
by a causal target query. Each operation couples an identification route to a specific estimator,
uncertainty construction and rejection condition. The initial release should not expose an
unqualified universal fit/predict abstraction for all seven.
   Published banking work illustrates why these distinctions matter. Within-bank deposit
comparisons isolate a different margin from within-county lending comparisons (Drechsler
et al., 2017). Comparing lenders to the same borrower can remove a stipulated common
demand shock but restricts the population to matched borrowers (Mian and Khwaja, 2006).
Eligibility-based refinancing comparisons distinguish a program effect from effects among
those who take it up (Agarwal et al., 2020). Regional effects need not recover aggregate


                                               1
2                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


monetary effects (Beraja et al., 2019). A structural mortgage model adds demand, supply and
capital-cost restrictions to answer a different counterfactual (Benetton, 2021). The product
preserves those differences; it does not transfer their published coefficients to a new bank.
Chapter 2

Three workspaces and one scientific
library

2.1     Intervention studies
An analyst registers eligibility, assignment, receipt, follow-up, the financial account and the
comparison population. The workspace reconstructs what was available at each decision, shows
the causal diagram and identification route, and estimates only the supported target. A rollout
can use cohort-specific effects under a named parallel-trend restriction; a randomized invitation
can report ITT and, under additional restrictions, a compliance-weighted effect. The analyst
sees effect heterogeneity and sensitivity alongside the aggregate economic account.
   This workspace is the natural entry point for deposit offers, marketing, branch changes and
credit interventions. FinMarketing could consume its study and result objects. The interface
must preserve direction, eligibility, currency, horizon, treatment version and sampling units.
That integration is specified; it has not been implemented in the sibling repository.


2.2     Sequential decisions
The analyst specifies a policy that uses only information available before each action, with
eligibility, censoring and competing outcomes explicit. For an observed-history identification
route, the workspace evaluates the longitudinal intervention using cumulative assignment ratios
and backward continuation models. It separates evaluation of a frozen policy from selection of
a new policy.
   For partial observation, the model must declare state transition, observation, reward and
behavior-assignment mechanisms. If a historical decision maker used private information about
latent distress, the observed action contains information about that distress. Dropping this
logger from the likelihood can reverse the estimated value of assistance. Planning then needs
an interventional transition law and a filtered belief based on permitted information, not a
state smoothed using future outcomes. The belief-state dynamic program is conditional on
that model (Kaelbling et al., 1998); solving it does not identify the model from bank records.
   BayesFilter could supply qualified filtering or numerical components for specified likelihoods.
The causal library would retain assignment and intervention semantics. A general unknown-
emission nonlinear POMDP estimator with causal guarantees is outside the proposed first
release.



                                                3
4                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


2.3     Dynamic systems
An economist registers series vintages, timing, shock normalization, instruments and structural
restrictions. The workspace compares panel, local-projection and state-space constructions
with their respective inference and identification limits. Calendar shocks and repeated entities
require a sampling construction appropriate to the dependence.
   Discovery contributes candidate equivalence graphs and refutable restrictions. Under latent
confounding, unresolved graph endpoints remain unresolved; they are propagated into target
queries or effect sets. Generalized adjustment applies only within its stated graph classes
(Perković et al., 2018). Stability under resampling is not a posterior probability that an arrow
is causal.
   MacroFinance could consume identified or explicitly restricted shock response objects;
dataml could provide qualified data and nuisance-learning components. Those applications
retain their substantive models. All four sibling integrations are proposed contracts, with no
claim of completed adoption or runtime compatibility.
Chapter 3

What the existing evidence does and
does not show

The additional bounded constructions expose the information needed for broader support.
Persistent customer maps receive one audit contribution per complete pair; representative audits
reveal linked outcomes rather than merely counting correctness. Joint response projection
can narrow strong-linkage sets while retaining weak and singular ambiguity. A nonlinear
private-logger likelihood is identified through independent state-labelled audits and evaluates an
independently trained observable policy. A finite latent temporal class preserves effect ambiguity
unless validated experimental or measurement information justifies narrower restrictions.
   The initial nonlinear parameter domain caused many unavailable boundary intervals. A
fresh stable-domain and larger-audit comparison improves availability and yields 95 covering
intervals out of 100 in its larger-audit arm, with substantial Monte Carlo uncertainty. It remains
a selected model-conditional reference, not general POMDP qualification. False audit selection
probabilities and false graph exclusions remain severe adverse examples. Public consumers
retain those qualifications. Local restart tests preserve score accounting after interruption,
while fitted matrices still materialize and multi-host performance remains unmeasured.
   The reliability extension separates persistent customer identities, common calendar shocks
and independent label-validation information. The first joint design under-covers at .9217; a
fresh larger design reaches .94, with Monte Carlo uncertainty including .95. Audit allocation
produces only a small standard-error reduction at matched expected cost, and more audits
cannot remove the common-calendar precision floor. Fresh dynamic funding calibration remains
uneven (.936, .948 and .918 across three designs); larger samples or covariance windows alone
are not a demonstrated universal repair.
   Exact Gaussian effect-test inversion gives narrower useful confidence sets under valid en-
couragement or observed sufficiency, while weak information retains whole-line or disconnected
answers and false exclusion gives zero coverage. An audited action-dependent nonlinear
transition variance model supplies 115 covering intervals in 120 correct-model requests; the
homogeneous challenger achieves the same count, and an omitted transition term leaves all
requests unqualified. A richer dependent dictionary removes one omitted- interaction bias and
fits through chunked QR, but original coverage is .9033; a larger registered design reaches .94.
A new omitted feature again destroys coverage. Complete local workload comparisons show
numerical agreement, small memory reductions and no consistent speed gain. These selected
results prepare concrete independent-review, bank-data, interface, workflow and platform
protocols; they do not constitute external acceptance or savings.
  Funding calibration now has a more explicit information account. In the selected model,


                                                5
6                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


an exact calculation isolates the target shift caused by a finite independent pilot and shows
why its size must grow relative to the evaluation sample. A fixed joint-regression alternative
under-covers at 720 dates, so that failure remains visible. A fresh fourfold-pilot comparison
covers .960, .942 and .933 across three designs; Monte Carlo intervals include .95, but matched
comparisons do not establish clear superiority. The larger designs require three or twelve times
the earlier pilot history, whose acquisition is unpriced.
   For the separate joint-regression route, fitting and scalar covariance can be computed in two
passes without retaining every score. At 1.2 million dates, complete local requests use about
43 percent of dense peak memory and 83–84 percent of dense elapsed time, with numerical
agreement. The original growing-pilot implementation stores its arrays. These improvements
justify a bounded reference capability and further independent challenge; they do not supply
a bank assignment design, accepted integration, target-platform service level or measured
analyst savings.
   A more precise comparison adds 2,000 fresh requests in each of eight selected designs. With
small identity audits, all three fixed procedures remain below nominal coverage even after
adjustment for the 24 marginal comparisons. Near-singular linkage allows intervals in only
451 of 2,000 requests; false exogeneity causes severe failure. At 1,200 dates the pilots have
selected-design evidence of better coverage than joint regression, but doubling independent
pilot history from fourfold to eightfold gives no clear further benefit. The larger history remains
a real, unpriced information requirement.
   An equivalent streaming pilot now preserves chronological penalty selection, full-pilot fitting
and financial uncertainty. Complete local requests with 120,000 evaluation dates and 480,000
pilot dates use 54–60 percent of the dense peak memory. Time ratios of .91 and 1.07 show no
consistent speed gain. This narrows the storage limitation of the selected implementation; it
does not establish general calibration, independent bank validity or analyst savings.
  The known-truth numerical studies use fully specified synthetic laws, fixed seeds and
preserved results. They test adverse comparisons as well as favorable examples. A separate
public 401(k) study has unknown causal truth. Neither provides estimates for JPMorgan
Chase, Bank of America, HSBC or any other institution.

   In the collections experiment, the main augmented estimator covers the true fixed-policy
value in .9375 of 160 replications. A deliberately wrong continuation model with correct
assignment probabilities covers only .86875. Double robustness of the population score is not
a finite-sample coverage guarantee. The hidden-state study records capped fits, multiple starts
and a longer convergence check. Its joint and omitted likelihoods refer to different statistical
experiments and are not naively comparable by their raw log-likelihood values.
   Two local reusable components have narrower verified roles. The temporal component
chooses available revisions before applying economic windows. The score reducer preserves
global centering and entity/date intersections. In three fresh processes per size, the median
ten-million-row workload for two precomputed score coordinates takes about 1.19 seconds and
peaks at about 123 MiB. It excludes data loading, temporal reconstruction, nuisance learning
and latent-model fitting. It is a bounded component measurement, not end-to-end bank-scale
throughput.
   The expanded response study derives joint inference over 26 outcome/horizon coordinates.
Across 500 replications, the default joint band covers in .958 of a strong, uncorrelated-
instrument-noise case but only .818 near the unit boundary. A separate integrated-series
construction reaches .966 coverage; naively treating levels as stationary reaches .586. These
findings support explicit persistence regimes and bandwidth comparisons, not a universal
confidence-band default.
   Unknown-emission controlled identification is matched to the model fitted. In 100
randomized-logging replications, fixed-policy value intervals cover in .96; an omitted private-
state logger gives zero coverage over 60 runs. The discovery construction carries a covariance
confidence region through a finite graph class to an outer effect set. A hidden common cause
defeats its causal-sufficiency assumption even when the observed covariance is accurately
estimated. Automatic observation construction consequently retains alternative clocks,
aggregations and entity maps when the records cannot distinguish them.
   Complete fresh-process workloads now include local data reconstruction, fitting, uncertainty
and reporting. The largest response case processes 3.85 million versioned records in a median
3.38 seconds with about 717 MiB peak memory. A 3,200-customer, twelve-decision latent
analysis with 19 bootstrap refits takes 48.27 seconds; those 19 draws measure cost and do not
provide precise 95% quantiles. These are three-run local synthetic measurements, not bank
service guarantees or evidence of labor savings.
   The broad software review retains 44 source/document qualifications. Selected installed
data-engine, sparse-learning and optimization operations also have version-bound executable
checks. Six bounded standalone study recipes and local mappings from the four inspected
sibling APIs demonstrate the richer scientific contracts. A source contract, a successful local
operation and accepted institutional integration remain different evidence.
   The expanded method comparisons change the proposed release priorities. For 26-coordinate
external-IV response sets, a longer covariance window raises near-unit coverage from .758 to
.933 in one prespecified experiment; prefiltering reaches .775. All three fail with an invalid
instrument. A separate lag-augmented projection concerns a reduced-form target and cannot
silently replace that instrumented response. In short dynamic panels, system-GMM joint
8                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


coverage collapses to .033 or zero after violating its additional initial-condition restriction,
while the differenced reference remains near .95. These findings support a declared primary
method and substantive challenger, with their target and assumption differences visible.
   For continuous observed histories, fitted action and censoring models plus backwards
continuation regressions give .958 coverage across 120 repetitions; ignoring dropout gives .833.
The evaluated candidate policy was learned in a separate randomized pilot and frozen before
evaluation. Reward-dependent unobserved dropout lowers the full method’s coverage to .892,
so data organization cannot silently certify a censoring assumption.
   A privately logged three-state model now has a constructive identification route using
independently labelled, invariant emissions. Its joint value intervals cover only .850–.875, and
17 of 199 bootstrap refits fail or hit a boundary; that bootstrap interval is withheld. This route
remains a research fit. An exactly Gaussian continuous-state reference retains the private
action likelihood and attains .9625 coverage in 160 repetitions, under known noise laws and
calibrated measurement scale. It provides an exact numerical benchmark, not a guarantee
for a nonlinear bank POMDP. The 600-trajectory finite-state interval remains unqualified. A
separate 3,000-trajectory regime with 600 emission labels gives available intervals in all 120
runs and .942 coverage on the same mechanism. An alternative representative whole-trajectory
audit supports simpler count-based fitting: at 1,200 audited customers, a four-decision belief
policy trained on an independent pilot has .950 coverage in 400 runs. At 300 customers, sparse
categories make 54 of 400 fits unavailable. These are evidence-design choices, not a universal
sample-size threshold. Accurate predecision labels are essential: a registered 10% label-error
sensitivity gives zero coverage. The initial product can support these bounded finite-state
designs with explicit measurement requirements, alongside observed-history and restricted
Gaussian routes. Arbitrary nonlinear private-state uncertainty remains research.
  Temporal search now runs PCMCI+ and LPCMCI at a recorded Tigramite version. A
bounded adapter carries compatible sufficient-graph orders into fresh-data response curves,
and refuses endpoint types it cannot interpret. A two-series Gaussian example gives an
impact envelope from zero to about .61 despite equivalent observational laws. A price
experiment or reliable timing restriction could resolve that ambiguity. Generated observation
candidates likewise require truthful metadata answers; unsupported keys cause incompatibility.
A representative independent linkage audit raises coverage from zero to .955 in a separate
synthetic example, whereas a biased audit gives only .015. More precise computation does not
repair wrong semantics.
  The public financial application uses 9,915 households, preserving eligibility and participation
as different causal variables (Chernozhukov et al., 2018; DMLonGitHub application-data
repository, 2026). Across two nuisance families and three splits, adjusted eligibility ATEs
range from about USD 7,968 to USD 8,932; participation LATEs range from USD 11,398 to
USD 12,935 under additional IV assumptions. These are archived dollars and an iid working
analysis; the extract lacks survey-design fields and cannot verify unmeasured selection or
control timing. Matched DoubleML 0.11.4 calls agree with the independent score to numerical
precision (doubleml contributors, 2026). This demonstrates reproducible composition, not
empirical proof of the identifying assumptions.
   Larger complete local workloads expose the dominant costs. Six latent states, 3,000
trajectories, 24 decisions and three refits take 122–133 seconds. Temporal search with 24
variables, eight lags and 6,400 dates takes 51–102 seconds. These are two fresh processes per case
with one verified numerical thread, including local data handling and reporting. Three refits
measure cost rather than confidence tails. Whole-customer batching, date-boundary covariance
terms and staged graph search require different execution plans; distributed throughput and
analyst-time savings remain unmeasured.
                                                                                                 9


   The latest common treasury construction carries delayed balance revisions, two candidate
entity histories, an independent linkage audit, pilot-trained controls, common-calendar response
covariance and financial accounting in one workflow. Two consumers reuse the same result: a
treasury report and an application-level per-account account. Margin changes recompute the
financial result; stock/flow substitutions and incompatible sampling laws are rejected. Serial
and partitioned calibration, fitting and covariance agree with an independent reference. At the
tested dimensions, serial execution is faster; the proposal does not claim a distributed speedup.
   Weak entity calibration changes what that financial result can mean. A separate procedure
projects response and audit confidence regions through the assignment model, retaining
unbounded or disconnected sets. In five 400-run synthetic regimes its sets cover every retained
truth, but weak and exactly singular assignments yield the whole real line in every run. Even
the strong regime has median projected width about 1.50 million currency units around a true
value of .375 million; its narrower regular interval covers .925 of runs. These are conservative
or imperfect finite-regime results, not a promised precise business case. The product must
expose the information shortfall and whether stronger identifiers, representative audits or a
portfolio-sum target could resolve it. Missing audits, unsupported response inputs and changes
of inference procedure have explicit result or rejection behavior; neither a failed calculation
nor a set-valued answer becomes a fabricated point estimate.
   The discovery comparison now uses the appropriate latent ancestral margin. Population-
oracle queries agree, but only about 66% of definite endpoint claims are correct in the finite-data
test despite nearly perfect adjacency precision. A learned causal ordering therefore remains
exploratory. Explicit front-door restrictions identify a separate hidden-variable query; a two-
model witness shows why a general confounded action/outcome query remains unresolved.
Better graph scoring does not manufacture identification.
   A preserved 203-quarter monetary dataset supplies a dynamic empirical sensitivity analysis
(statsmodels dataset contributors, 2026). The four-quarter M1 projection response differs
markedly before and after 1984. Quarterly rate averages, end-quarter stocks and missing private
policy information prevent interpreting that regression as a bank’s deposit-price intervention.
The central funding coverage experiments are consequently synthetic and explicit about their
assignment and observation laws. Public data provide an interpretation challenge, not known
causal truth.
Chapter 4

Construction and acceptance

The first tranche should put all three workspaces through a narrow end-to-end path. A
small multidisciplinary team combines causal econometrics, longitudinal/latent modeling, data
engineering, statistical computing and product design. Scientific review is scheduled explicitly;
it is not delegated to a successful software build.
   Months one and two establish the request/result objects, decision clocks, availability-
aware reconstruction and finite reference experiments. Months three and four implement a
limited adjusted/cohort operation, a frozen sequential-policy value operation, and a restricted
dynamic shock or graph-query operation. A controlled-state research path retains its explicit
identification assumptions. Months five and six compare those operations with the same
studies produced by expert composition, including review, rework and unsupported cases.
   Each adapter must preserve the target population, intervention direction, weights, clocks,
graph endpoints and sampling experiment. Acceptance includes finite identity checks;
incompatible-request rejection; small-case comparison with an independent implementation;
simulation under named adverse laws; and cost/latency measurements for the complete
workload. A result that is numerically plausible but represents a different target fails
acceptance.
   The scientific plan fixes the study and its folds. The physical execution plan chooses
partitioning, caching and scheduling while preserving that plan. Trajectory fits, common-
parameter EM, local projections, graph search and score reductions have different cost and
approximation behavior. Distributing rows is insufficient when clusters cross partitions. Scaling
claims must state their state dimension, horizon, population, dependence coordinates, storage
and approximation budget.
  The product can run inside a bank’s data boundary with local storage and controlled package
environments. A standalone application supplies study preparation, model comparison, review
and export; the same library objects serve other applications. Deployment, authentication,
entitlements, retention and operational monitoring remain engineering work. They do not
change the causal restrictions or turn an unsupported target into an estimate.

Chapter 5

Economics and stopping rules

Compare the product with a competent quantitative team assembling the same open-source
methods, historical data and review outputs. For alternative j, let Kj be initial cost, Fj annual
common cost, cj cost per equivalent completed study and nt annual volume. Present cost is
                                            H
                                                  (1 + r)−t (Fj + cj nt ).
                                            X
                               Cj = K j +
                                            t=1

An equivalent study includes a defensible identification or nonidentification result, appropriate
uncertainty and reproducible review. Failed work and rework must remain in the account.
   The illustrative USD-million inputs are expert composition (KE , FE , cE ) = (1, .6, .15) and
product (KP , FP , cP ) = (4, 1.8, .06), with three years and a 10% discount rate. They are
planning assumptions, not bank quotations or measured labor savings.

                   Scenario         Expert cost Platform cost Platform saving
                   Low reuse              5.476              9.670           -4.194
                   Moderate reuse        11.445             12.057           -0.613
                   High reuse            15.921             13.848            2.073
                   Adoption ramp          8.402             10.840           -2.438

Table 5.1: Equivalent-output present costs under the stipulated assumptions. The ramp has
annual study volumes 4, 16 and 30.

   The product costs USD 4.19 million more at eight annual studies and USD .61 million more
at 24; it saves USD 2.07 million at 36. The adoption ramp leaves a USD 2.44 million premium.
Constant-volume break-even is 26.74 studies annually, rising to 53.47 if marginal savings halve.
A broad bank balance sheet does not demonstrate sufficient reuse.
   The first-tranche envelope follows from six people for six months at an illustrative fully loaded
USD 25,000 per person-month, USD 50,000 of compute and tooling, and 20% contingency:
USD 1.14 million. This amount is included in the USD 4 million initial product cost, not added
to it. Data-owner, validation, security and application-owner participation are unpriced here
and must be costed consistently for both alternatives. Later tranches should be priced from
actual operation-specific effort and adoption evidence.
   Decision value must be incremental to the expert comparator. Saved analyst effort already
counted in study costs cannot be counted again as business benefit. At 24 annual studies,
closing the remaining cost premium requires about USD .246 million of additional annual
decision value; the ramp requires about USD .980 million. A synthetic finding that an offer


                                                    11
12                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


loses money does not establish that the product, rather than the expert team, causes the bank
to avoid that loss.
   The adoption experiment should assign comparable studies to both workflows, record
preparation/fitting/review time and rework, and compare analytical quality against a common
review standard. Track operation mix, unsupported requests, repeated reusable work and
changes to actual decisions. Continue construction only when the observed case supports
the cost of the next tranche. Reduce scope or stop if demand is mostly bespoke, semantic
errors persist, qualified outputs are no cheaper, or available data cannot identify the intended
policies.
   An independent commercial product additionally needs evidence of willingness to pay,
installation effort, support burden, release compatibility and procurement acceptance. Those
facts have not been measured here. The proposal establishes a bounded scientific design and a
way to test its investment case; commercial expansion follows that evidence.
